newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor hits new high on listing news.
newsitem.headline: Gencor hits new high on listing news.

text.p: Shares in South African mining house Gencor Ltd continued rallying to new highs at the start of trade on Thursday following news on Wednesday it was listing a new base metals firm in London and would raise $1 billion offshore.
By 0737 GMT Gencor had added 75 cents or over 3.6 percent to a new year high of 21.50 rand in volume of 102,300 shares.
"The news about the listing is very bullish," one dealer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.

"It gives Gencor full exposure to foreign currency-denominated earnings. The new firm will also be protected from the gold operations in South Africa which, together with the whole industry, have been undergoing some turmoil," the dealer added.
Gencor announced on Wednesday that it will be listing a new base metals company Billiton Plc on the London Stock Exchange and raising more than $1 billion through a global equity placement.

"Billiton will be one of the largest and lowest cost producers of aluminium and the leading producer of ferroalloys, the world's largest exporter of thermal coal and a leading source of titanium minerals," the company said in a statement.
Following the announcement Gencor shares on Wednesday soared to a 1997 high of 21.10 rand. Shares gained 8.6 percent or 165 cents overall on the day to finish at 20.75 rand.

Alongside this news, investors were also digesting comments from the firm that it expected an improvement in earnings in the current quarter to end-June and continued to expect similar second-half results to those achieved in the first half.
Gencor also said it was expecting to make a decision by the end of June on whether to begin construction of the $1.25 billion Mozal aluminium smelter near Maputo.
